Practical questions

The ordinary practical things

Service times, where to sit, how to follow along, and who to telephone. Most of these are answered somewhere else on this site as well, and each card says where.

When are services?

Every Sunday: Orthros at 9:00 a.m., Divine Liturgy at 10:00 a.m. Weekday and feast-day services are on the calendar.

Sunday morning is Orthros at 9:00 a.m., followed by the Divine Liturgy at 10:00 a.m. They are two distinct services; people arrive across both.

Feasts, Paraklesis and the services of Holy Week are kept as they fall, so the parish calendar is the place to check.

What is Orthros?

The morning service that comes before the Divine Liturgy. Here it begins at 9:00 a.m.

Orthros is the Church's morning prayer — psalms, hymns for the day, and the Gospel of the Resurrection on a Sunday. It leads straight into the Divine Liturgy without a break, which is why the two can sound like one long service.

You are not late if you arrive during it, and you are not late if you arrive after it either.

Answer last reviewed 13 August 2026

What is the Divine Liturgy?

The Sunday service of the Church, at whose heart is Holy Communion. Here it begins at 10:00 a.m.

The Divine Liturgy is the central service of the Orthodox Church: scripture, prayer and hymns leading to the offering of the Eucharist. Most Sundays here it is the Liturgy of St. John Chrysostom.

Services are approximately 50% Greek and 50% English, and congregational portions — the Creed, the Lord's Prayer — are offered in more than one language.

Where should I sit?

Anywhere. There is no reserved seating.

There is no reserved seating. Sit where you like — towards the back is easy if you would rather watch before joining in, and nobody will move you on.

People come and go a little during Orthros, and stand and sit at different moments. Follow along if you want to; sit when you need to.

How do I follow the service book?

Take a Greek-English Divine Liturgy book from a greeter or from the pew. It stays in the church.

A Greek-English Divine Liturgy book is available from a greeter or in the pew, with the service in both languages side by side. It stays in the church at the end of the service.

Following it is easier than it looks, and losing your place is normal. Much of the Liturgy repeats week to week, and you will know it sooner than you expect.

What does “Kyrie eleison” mean?

“Lord, have mercy.”

Kyrie eleison — “Lord, have mercy.” You will hear this response again and again throughout Orthodox worship.

Even if you know no other Greek, it probably won't be long before you recognise it.

Answer last reviewed 13 August 2026

What happens at coffee hour?

Everyone goes down to the hall and eats together. That is most of it.

After the Divine Liturgy the parish gathers in the parish hall for coffee hour — a shared, potluck-style meal, and an old Christian habit of sitting down to eat together after worship.

It is where the parish actually meets, and it is the easiest place to ask a question you did not want to ask in church.

How do I find out about classes and events?

The parish calendar, the weekly bulletin, and The Light — the parish's monthly newsletter.

The parish calendar carries the services and the parish events. The Light, the parish's monthly newsletter, carries what is coming and what has happened, and the weekly bulletin is posted online each week.

Announcements are also made at the end of the Liturgy, which is a good reason not to leave immediately.
